subject: Physics
subtopic: Magnetic fields, Lorentz force and electromagnetic induction
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate. It is never a learner estimate, and Core1A/Core1B may not consult one.

rungs.aha: Magnetic field B is an axial vector: its direction is tied to an oriented rotation convention, and dot/cross marks encode out-of-page and into-page directions rather than particle paths.
learner_owns: Can distinguish a location in a diagram from a direction assigned at that location.
must_contain: Arrow, dot, and cross conventions bound explicitly to magnetic-field direction.
The axial-vector character of B stated separately from the polar-vector motion of a charged particle.
A closed-loop field-line picture that does not treat lines as material strings.

misconception.wrong_idea: Magnetic field lines begin at a north pole and end at a south pole everywhere.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Trace one magnetic field line through and around a bar magnet. Where can it stop?
misconception.repair: Treat field lines as a direction map: they continue in closed loops, including through the magnet.

rungs.closure: Given dot/cross/arrows around a magnet, identify the local B direction, name its axial-vector convention, and state whether a field line may terminate there.

controlled_variation.vary: the viewing orientation of the same magnetic field
controlled_variation.hold: the physical B direction in space
controlled_variation.notice: dot, cross, and in-plane arrow are representation choices for one axial direction
the field direction changes continuously and the line closes rather than terminating

rungs.aha: Magnetic flux measures the component of magnetic field through an oriented area; changing the surface orientation changes flux even when B and area size stay fixed.
learner_owns: R1: magnetic field B is an axial directed quantity with explicit in-plane and out-of-plane representation conventions.
must_contain: An explicit area-normal direction before any cosine is used.
Comparison of face-on, tilted, and edge-on orientations at fixed B and area.

misconception.wrong_idea: Flux is just magnetic-field strength times area, so orientation does not matter.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A loop with fixed area rotates from face-on to edge-on in a uniform field. What must happen to its flux?
misconception.repair: Project the oriented area along the field direction: the dot product selects the component through the surface.

rungs.closure: Rank the flux for several orientations of the same loop in one uniform field and justify the ranking from the area normal.

controlled_variation.vary: the angle between B and the area normal
controlled_variation.notice: flux changes from maximum to zero without changing B or area

controlled_variation.vary: the chosen normal orientation for the same physical surface
controlled_variation.notice: the signed flux reverses with the normal while the physical surface is unchanged

rungs.aha: The magnetic force on a moving charge is set by q(v x B): it is perpendicular to both v and B, and its direction reverses for negative charge.
learner_owns: R2: magnetic flux depends on an oriented area and on the direction of B, not only their magnitudes.
must_contain: A three-direction construction: v, B, then v x B.
A separate sign step for the charge after the right-hand direction is found.

misconception.wrong_idea: The right-hand rule gives the force direction for both positive and negative charges without any extra step.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A positive and a negative charge enter the same field with the same velocity. Do they bend to the same side?
misconception.repair: First find v x B for a positive charge; then reverse that direction if q is negative.

rungs.closure: Given v, B, and the sign of q in a dot/cross diagram, determine the magnetic-force direction and identify the zero-force orientations.

controlled_variation.vary: the angle between velocity and magnetic field
controlled_variation.hold: charge sign, speed, and field magnitude
controlled_variation.notice: force is zero when v is parallel to B and largest when they are perpendicular
force direction reverses while magnitude stays the same

rungs.aha: A pure magnetic force can bend a charged particle without changing its speed because the force is perpendicular to instantaneous velocity and does zero work.
learner_owns: R3: magnetic-force direction follows q(v x B) and is perpendicular to velocity.
must_contain: A velocity arrow before and after a short time step with equal lengths.
A work or power check using F dot v.

misconception.wrong_idea: A magnetic field makes a charged particle speed up because a force acts on it.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: An electron curves in a uniform magnetic field. If its speed rises, where did the extra kinetic energy come from?
misconception.repair: Compare force with velocity: perpendicular force redirects motion, while zero F dot v means no magnetic work.

rungs.closure: Given a particle trajectory in a uniform pure magnetic field, distinguish what can change (direction) from what cannot (speed and kinetic energy).

controlled_variation.vary: elapsed time along a curved trajectory
controlled_variation.hold: uniform B and no electric field
controlled_variation.notice: the velocity direction changes while its magnitude stays fixed

controlled_variation.hold: particle charge and initial speed, with v perpendicular to B
controlled_variation.notice: the curvature changes but the speed does not

rungs.aha: Induced emf responds to change in magnetic flux, and its direction opposes the change rather than simply opposing the magnetic field.
learner_owns: R4: pure magnetic force can redirect motion without changing speed or kinetic energy.
must_contain: Two cases with the same external-field direction but opposite flux changes.
A stated cause of flux change: field magnitude, area, or orientation.

misconception.wrong_idea: Lenz's law says the induced field always points opposite to the external magnetic field.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A north pole approaches a loop and then retreats. Should the induced current direction stay the same?
misconception.repair: Name the flux change first; choose the induced effect that resists that change, not the field itself.

rungs.closure: Given whether magnetic flux through a loop is increasing or decreasing, determine the induced field/current sense and explain the opposition.

controlled_variation.vary: whether the external flux is increasing or decreasing
controlled_variation.hold: the external-field direction and loop orientation
controlled_variation.notice: the induced direction reverses because the change reverses

controlled_variation.vary: whether flux changes through field magnitude or loop orientation
controlled_variation.hold: the same signed rate of flux change
controlled_variation.notice: the induced emf depends on flux change, not on which mechanism produced it

rungs.aha: A conductor moving through a magnetic field develops motional emf because magnetic force separates charges; the simple Blv form requires the geometry to make the relevant directions perpendicular.
learner_owns: R5: induced emf direction is fixed by opposition to a change in magnetic flux.
must_contain: The conductor length direction, motion direction, and B direction shown together.
A statement of the perpendicular geometry before using Blv.

misconception.wrong_idea: The motional-emf magnitude is Blv for any orientation of conductor, velocity, and magnetic field.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A rod moves parallel to the magnetic field with speed v. Should the same Blv value appear as when it moves perpendicular to B?
misconception.repair: Return to q(v x B): only the force component along the conductor separates charge end-to-end.

rungs.closure: Given rod, v, and B directions, decide whether motional emf is zero or nonzero and use Blv only in the perpendicular geometry.

controlled_variation.vary: the angle between velocity and magnetic field
controlled_variation.hold: rod length, speed magnitude, field magnitude, and rod orientation
controlled_variation.notice: charge separation vanishes when v is parallel to B

controlled_variation.vary: rod orientation relative to v x B
controlled_variation.hold: v and B perpendicular with fixed magnitudes
controlled_variation.notice: end-to-end emf depends on whether magnetic force has a component along the rod

family.invariant_demand: Identify the directed geometry, choose whether the situation calls for force or flux-change reasoning, determine direction before magnitude, and check the result against perpendicularity or energy conservation.
family.difficult_move: Reading the three-dimensional direction information correctly before applying a right-hand or Lenz-law rule.
family.independent_check: For pure magnetic force, F must be perpendicular to v and cannot change kinetic energy; for induction, the predicted response must oppose the stated flux change.

support_ladder.handed_over: The relevant vectors are labeled and the applicable rule (force or flux change) is named.
The vectors and their dot/cross page conventions are labeled, but the learner chooses the rule and direction.
Only the physical situation and diagram are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: A charged particle enters crossed electric and magnetic fields, so decide which effects can change speed and which only redirect motion.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that the electric-force term can do work while the magnetic term cannot

transfer.changed_demand: Convert a dot/cross field diagram and a loop orientation into signed magnetic flux and an induced-current direction.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the area-normal direction implied by the drawing

transfer.changed_demand: Analyze a moving conducting rail or generator segment instead of a free charged particle.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which direction of magnetic force separates charge along the conductor

transfer.changed_demand: Use magnetic force as the centripetal force to relate a particle's path radius to q, v, B, and mass.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the step equating qvB with the required centripetal-force magnitude
